title: Patch: a pull request that changes only the mutation-testing settings or scripts no longer runs the CI jobs that never read them
thread:
**Issue #4112 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4112: Patch: a pull request that changes only the mutation-testing settings or scripts no longer runs the CI jobs that never read them
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The project has a weekly mutation-testing run, with its own settings file and scripts. The script that picks which checks a pull request needs gets them wrong: it takes the settings file for a build setting, and the scripts for something the website reads. So a pull request touching them runs almost every check: the engine's and the AI's test groups, the web's unit shards, the end-to-end smoke. None of those checks reads these files.

Such pull requests are common, because the ongoing mutation audit edits the settings file with every batch. Every needless check waits in the same queue as everyone else's work. Once this is built:
- a pull request that changes the shared crate and the settings file runs the checks the shared crate needs, as it would without the settings file;
- a pull request that changes only the mutation scripts runs none of the heavy checks. The mutation workflow still tests it on its own.

## Why
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh:291` reads `Cargo.toml | Cargo.lock | rust-toolchain.toml | .cargo/* | .github/* | scripts/ci-scope.sh)` and turns on `clippy $RUST web web_promote e2e`. `.cargo/*` is there for `.cargo/config.toml`, which cargo reads. `.cargo/mutants.toml` is cargo-mutants' own file, which no build reads; only `scripts/mutants.sh` and `.github/workflows/mutants.yml` name it.
- `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh` and `scripts/pool-probe.sh` fall through to `*) on web` and `*) on e2e`. The e2e case lists the scripts no build runs (`browse.sh`, the two promote scripts, `server-image.sh`, `worktree.sh`) and leaves these three out.
- No `ci.yml` job runs any of them: `grep mutants .github/workflows/ci.yml` finds nothing. The code that names them does so only in comments (`crates/engine/src/testkit/pool_probe.rs:7`, `crates/run/src/tests.rs:987`, the two Stryker configs).
- `mutants.yml`'s `pull_request.paths` already list `.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh` and `scripts/mutants-runner.sh`, so a change to them keeps a check that does read them.
- Since 2026-10-01, `.cargo/mutants.toml` changed in 18 commits on `main`. In 13 of them, every other file sat under `crates/shared/` or `crates/run/`, or was `scripts/mutants.sh`. These are the #3513 and #3593 audit batches: 317174aa76, 11274b4844, e4f70ffd2f, c4fbb5d7ae, f65478fb79, e41b3d174c, eb59ecbd78, 562883049a, 63d7b1a286, 4ff211a4e3, a98affd22b, 48a8587363, bd47844434.
  - For a `crates/shared` change, the crate map runs `rust_server` and `rust_tools_wasm`.
  - The settings file added the three engine rules jobs, `engine`, `engine golden`, `cards lib`, `cards`, `ai`, `ai slow` and `web (promote-production)`, each compiling on its own.
  - bd47844434 changed only `mutants.toml` and `mutants.sh`, and ran every Rust group, every web job and all four e2e smoke shards.
  - #4038 (open) will edit `mutants.sh` again.
- CLAUDE.md, CI: every push runs on the organization's shared runners, and the runner gate lets only six CI and CD runs go at once, pull requests last.

## Proposal
- Add `.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh` and `scripts/pool-probe.sh` to `ci-scope.sh`'s skip list (`skipped()`), as a new class in the header's description of the list: the mutation-testing tooling, which `mutants.yml` runs and checks on its own trigger, and the pool probe, which a person runs.
- Restate in the header the proof that nothing in `crates/`, `apps/`, `e2e/` or `spec/` reads these files, as CLAUDE.md asks of a path joining the list.
- The effect: a diff of only those files runs `bot selftest` alone in `ci.yml`, beside `mutants.yml`'s own run. Beside other files they are skipped, and the diff scopes as those files do.
- Leave the rest as it is: `.cargo/config.toml` and every other `.cargo/` file keep running every job. `.github/mutants-floor.txt` and `mutants.yml` keep running everything, as all of `.github/` does, and `ci-scope.test.ts` pins the floor file.
- Update the header's lines on what `.cargo/` and the scripts turn on.

Rejected alternative: a case that turns on no line but leaves `full` true. A diff of mutation tooling alone would still run the release builds, `rust (checks, fuzz 200)` and `rust (classify)`, none of which reads it.

## Where it lands
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (the skip list and its header)
- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In `ci-scope.test.ts`, each of the four files alone, and each beside `bot/harness/state.py`, gives `full=false`. This fails on today's script.
- [ ] `crates/shared/src/lib.rs` beside `.cargo/mutants.toml` turns on exactly the lines `crates/shared/src/lib.rs` alone does. Likewise, `crates/run/src/lib.rs` beside `scripts/mutants.sh` turns on exactly what `crates/run/src/lib.rs` alone does. Both fail today.
- [ ] `.cargo/config.toml` still runs every job but the db suites (the existing cargo-settings test passes unchanged), and `.github/mutants-floor.txt` still runs everything.
- [ ] The tests that hold the script to the paths the web's and e2e's sources name still pass.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] The header names the four paths and why each is on the list.

## Size and risks
- **Size:** small, **difficulty:medium**: about 10 lines of script and 20 of test.
- **Timing:** it takes effect on the pull requests after it lands, since `ci.yml`'s `changes` job runs `main`'s copy of the script (#2986). The pull request that makes it runs everything.
- **Risk:** a later CI job that starts reading one of these files must take it off the list in the same pull request; the header says so. A push to `main` and the daily super run still run everything, whatever changed.

Area: `tests` (`suggestions.areas`).

Class: `checks` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

## Goal

A pull request that changes only the mutation-testing tooling (`.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh`) or the pool probe (`scripts/pool-probe.sh`) scopes to `full=false`, so `ci.yml` runs only `bot selftest` beside `mutants.yml`'s own run. Beside other files those four are skipped and the diff scopes as the other files do. Everything else (`.cargo/config.toml`, `.github/mutants-floor.txt`, the rest of `.cargo/`, all other scripts) keeps today's scope.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-scope.sh` | change | One new case line in `skipped()`; header: new skip-list class paragraph, and updated lines on what `.cargo/` and the scripts turn on |
| `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` | change | Three new `it` blocks: four-files skip, shared-beside-mutants.toml, run-beside-mutants.sh |

Do not touch anything else: not `mutants.yml` (its `pull_request.paths` already covers three of the four), not `.cargo/config.toml`, not `.github/mutants-floor.txt`, not any crate, app, `e2e/`, or `spec/` file. No spec section or ruling governs this change; the proof the header must restate is the grep result in Steps.

## Steps

1. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, function `skipped()`, add one case line immediately before `*) return 1 ;;` (after the `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml) ;;` line), matching the bare style of the surrounding lines (no comment; the header carries the explanation):
   `.cargo/mutants.toml | scripts/mutants.sh | scripts/mutants-runner.sh | scripts/pool-probe.sh) ;;`
   Make no other body change. Skipped files `continue` in the per-file loop before any `on` case, so `.cargo/*` (run-everything line), `*) on web`, and `*) on e2e` can no longer catch them.
2. In the same file's header, extend the skip-list paragraph (the block ending "but for the five record files and reports of `analysis/fixtures/`") with a new class: the mutation-testing tooling, which `mutants.yml` runs and checks on its own trigger (`.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh`), and the pool probe (`scripts/pool-probe.sh`), which a person runs. Add the header's required warning: a later CI job that starts reading one of these files must take it off the list in the same pull request.
3. In the same header, update the run-everything paragraph ("Run everything but the db suites: the workspace's `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.cargo/`, ...") so `.cargo/` reads `.cargo/ but .cargo/mutants.toml`, and update the `clippy` paragraph ("any Rust source, manifest, lockfile, clippy.toml, rustfmt.toml, the toolchain or `.cargo/`") the same way.
4. In the same header, update the `e2e` paragraph's "the scripts no build runs" line so it names the scripts that stay off-e2e after this change: `scripts/browse.sh`, `scripts/promote-production.sh`, `scripts/promote-staging.sh`, `scripts/server-image.sh`, `scripts/worktree.sh` (the four mutation/pool-probe scripts no longer reach that case).
5. In `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, after the "skips the heavy jobs for a diff of the night bot's own files and nothing else" test, add `it("skips the heavy jobs for a diff of only the mutation-testing tooling or the pool probe", ...)`: for each of `.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh`, `scripts/pool-probe.sh`, assert `onFor(file)` is `[]` and `onFor("bot/harness/state.py", file)` is `[]`. Copy the `onFor(...)).toEqual([])` pattern from the existing skip test.
6. In the same test file add `it("scopes a shared-crate change beside .cargo/mutants.toml as the shared crate alone", ...)`: assert `answerFor(".cargo/mutants.toml")` equals `every(false)`, and `answerFor("crates/shared/src/lib.rs", ".cargo/mutants.toml")` equals `answerFor("crates/shared/src/lib.rs")` (equality form, not a hardcoded array, so later map changes do not brittle it). Note for the builder: today's script gives shared-alone as full, db, db_store, db_deploy, clippy, rust_server, rust_tools_wasm, web, e2e (probed), and shared-beside adds every engine/AI group plus web_promote — that is the bug this test pins.
7. In the same test file add the run pairing: assert `answerFor("scripts/mutants.sh")` equals `every(false)`, and `answerFor("crates/run/src/lib.rs", "scripts/mutants.sh")` equals `answerFor("crates/run/src/lib.rs")`. Note for the builder: the beside-equality already holds today (probed: both give full, clippy, rust_server, rust_tools_wasm, web, e2e, since `mutants.sh` alone adds only web+e2e which the run file already turns on); this test fails today on the alone assertion and guards the pair against regressions. Do not alter the existing `.cargo/config.toml` cargo-settings test, the `.github/mutants-floor.txt` runs-everything row, or any `SCOPED`/`GROUPS`/scan test.

## Tests

- New tests, all in `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`: the four-files skip test (step 5), the shared-beside test (step 6), the run-beside test (step 7). Each pair's alone-assertion fails on today's script (probed: mutants.toml alone turns on full/clippy/all-RUST/web/web_promote/e2e; each script alone turns on full/web/e2e); the shared-beside equality fails today too.
- Unchanged tests that must keep passing: the cargo-settings test (`.cargo/config.toml` still turns on full, clippy, all RUST, web, web_promote, e2e), the runs-everything row holding `.github/mutants-floor.txt`, and the `WEB`/`E2E` named-paths scans (no source under `apps/web/src`, `e2e/`, or `apps/edge/src` names any of the four paths — grep exit 1 — and the Stryker configs that do are not scan roots, so those scans are unaffected).
- Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`.

## Done when

- [ ] The four files alone, and each beside `bot/harness/state.py`, give `full=false` (empty `onFor`).
- [ ] `crates/shared/src/lib.rs` beside `.cargo/mutants.toml` scopes exactly as without it; same for `crates/run/src/lib.rs` beside `scripts/mutants.sh`.
- [ ] `.cargo/config.toml` and `.github/mutants-floor.txt` scope exactly as today; the web/e2e named-paths tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] The vitest file above passes; the header names all four paths and why each is listed.
- [ ] No file outside the two listed above changed.

## Risks

- A future CI job that reads one of the four files would silently skip while the file stays listed; the header warning from step 2 is the mitigation, per the script's own rule.
- `ci.yml`'s `changes` job runs `main`'s copy of the script, so this pull request itself still runs everything; the effect starts on later pull requests. That is expected, not a failure.
- A push to `main` and the daily super run always run everything regardless; untouched.

## Open questions

None.
```
